newsitem.title: USA: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - March 5.
newsitem.headline: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - March 5.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:

Comment - Many buyers remained on the sidelines, giving prices of several key lumber items a downward tilt, said Random Lengths in its midweek update. Uncertainty about the end of the Canadian quota year on March 31 cooled activity in spruce-pine-fir.
Canadian export quota used as of approximately February 25 was 66.4 percent of quarterly quota and 94.0 percent of the annual quota, said Random Lengths.

Weather restrained consumption in the Midwest and south. Wholesalers liquidated inventories. Plywood prices were firm to higher. Western S-P-F prices softened on most dimension items, but were supported by big discounts to random 2x4.

Canadian mills that had run out of quota focused on selling within Canada. But a few had not used up their annual allotments and continued to push for U.S. business. Standard and better 2x4's traded as low as $382.
Eastern S-P-F sales remained sluggish in U.S. markets. No. 1 and 2 2x4's and 2x6's were frequently subject to $5 counter offers; 2x8 and 2x10 prices were unchanged.
Buyers concentrated on mills with unfilled quotas, but looked for price concessions. Canadian markets were steady; wides were tight. Studs fell about $5, Random Lengths said.

Southern Pine sales were on the light side. Prices were mostly level, though No. 2 2x4s drifted lower in all producing zones. Heavy rains over the weekend continued to limit both logging and jobsite activity.

In dimension, producers frequently yielded to $5 to $10 counters to sell standard and better 2x4 and No. 2 and better 2x6, while the wides held firm. Stud prices held, with mills resisting counters. 12-inch boards remained tight, but upward price momentum slowed.

Coast Hem-Fir and dry Douglas fir sales stalled and several prices cracked. The narrows were weakest. Producers' order files shortened, and some mills built inventory on certain items. Hem-fir sales slowed due in part to weakness in spruce-pine-fir. Prices eroded $2 to $5, except for No.2 and better 2x12s. Fir prices lost $2 to $8.
